findings.claim: The refiner artifact was substantively mutated after its recorded terminate convergence with no new iteration entry, so the artifact that certifies 'exact evidence traceability' again misattributes post-termination work to the terminated iteration.
findings.evidence: state.json keeps iteration_history[0] as the sole iteration with "decision": "terminate", "timestamp": "2026-08-29T20:20:06Z", yet records "updated_at"/"finalized_at": "2026-08-29T21:06:46Z" and adds a checkpoint_authority block; refinement_log.md lists 'Added the machine checkpoint-authority marker, the JSON package-subpath ledger, and a canonical-state archive guard' under the heading 'Iteration 1 — 2026-08-29T20:15:30Z' even though those actions postdate the 20:20:06 termination (the archive guard's pre-gate receipt and correction receipt are stamped ≥20:38Z); registry.json finalized_at was re-stamped to 21:06:46Z. reflection.json still claims all blocking constraints 'pass with exact evidence traceability' for the blocking evidence-and-fixture-integrity constraint — the same chronology-falsification class flagged in rounds 1–3, recurring in the final artifact.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a second iteration (or an explicit post-termination amendment entry with its own timestamp) in iteration_history covering the checkpoint-marker, subpath-ledger, and archive-guard additions, so the chronology authority itself accurately describes when the final content was produced.

findings.claim: The round-7 fix inserted checkpoint_authority stale markers into the three current checkpoint files without updating their updated_at fields, so each file now falsely asserts it was last modified at its first-write time.
findings.evidence: checkpoints/45bed4e9.json contains the checkpoint_authority block ({"stale": true, "superseded_by": "../state.json"}) yet still claims "updated_at": "2026-08-29T20:20:06Z"; 9100ef56.json ("updated_at": "2026-08-29T20:20:05Z") and f0578e81.json ("updated_at": "2026-08-29T20:17:10Z") likewise embed the marker. resolution.md's Round 7 disposition states the markers were 'fixed inside each of the three affected current checkpoint files' — i.e., after round-7-findings.json, which itself postdates 20:38Z. A consumer trusting updated_at (the field the rounds 1–3 findings treated as the modification signal) will read these files as unmodified first writes.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump updated_at in each edited checkpoint file to the actual marker-insertion time, or add an explicit marker_inserted_at field, so the falsity-marker edit does not itself falsify the file's modification timestamp.

findings.claim: The new JSON-subpath ledger check builds package paths as path.join(root, "packages", selected.directory, ...), which double-prefixes 'packages/' if selected.directory follows the shared public-package inventory convention — either the check crashes with ENOENT or the pass claims in verification.md could not have been produced by this code.
findings.evidence: The hunk uses path.join(root, "packages", selected.directory, "package.json") and path.resolve(root, "packages", selected.directory, target). In the same scripts directory, package-contract-validation.mjs identifies the core package with publicPackage.directory === "packages/entity-graph-core" (hunk at line 67), i.e., the shared inventory's directory field already includes the 'packages/' prefix. If verify-skills-exports.mjs consumes the same inventory, the joined path is <root>/packages/packages/entity-graph-core/package.json and readFileSync throws before any comparison — yet verification.md asserts 'node scripts/verify-skills-exports.mjs --pkg core ... pass' and resolution.md Round 5 claims 'both fixture subpaths pass'. The packet contains no evidence resolving which inventory shape verify-skills-exports.mjs actually uses.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the definition of selected.directory in verify-skills-exports.mjs and align it with the package-contract-validation convention (use selected.directory directly if it already contains 'packages/'), and re-run the verifier capturing its output as receipt evidence.

findings.claim: The guard hashes final-packet.json but never parses or validates its contents, and assumes final-findings.json has a findings array, so malformed final artifacts fail with a raw TypeError or pass with an unexamined packet.
findings.evidence: The hunk does readFileSync(finalArtifactPaths.packet) and sha256(finalPacketBytes) without JSON.parse or any structural check, and calls finalFindings.findings.filter(...) unguarded — a findings file missing the findings field throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined' instead of an archive-guard diagnostic, contrary to the round-7 fix's stated goal of explicit guard diagnostics for final-artifact problems.
findings.suggested_fix: JSON.parse the packet and assert expected shape (e.g., mode/target fields), and guard the findings array with Array.isArray before filtering, emitting 'archive guard: final artifacts malformed' diagnostics.
